A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TR2C research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Visual inspection resolves the equation-extraction artifacts in v2, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TR2C experiments on five HMS datasets and three TAS datasets, including ablations, robustness tests, and representation analyses in the main text and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds comparisons with TAS methods on HMS datasets and experiments on computational scaling.

M1.justification: Equation (14) corrects L_rho from negative to positive one-half log-determinant, making the loss in Equation (13) consistent with Equation (9). The encoder, heads, affinity construction, and spectral clustering procedure remain unchanged. This establishes a correction to the stated loss, without establishing that implementations or experiments changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Weiz, Keck, UT, MAD, UCF-11 YouTube, Breakfast, YouTube Instructional, and 50 Salads. The new comparisons reuse Weiz and Keck; additional feature configurations and varying sequence sizes do not introduce new datasets, populations, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds TWF, ASOT, and HVQ as comparators against TR2C on Weiz and Keck. TWF and ASOT previously participated only in the TAS benchmark comparison, while HVQ is entirely new. This substantially extends the HMS comparison to TAS approaches; the comparator sets in Tables 2, 5, and 6 are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce DINOv2 ViT-L/14 features, best-result selection over TAS-method tuning grids in Table A.7, and timing measurements across N = 200–4000 with and without determinant commutation. Existing dataset preparation, evaluation metrics, and the previously documented training configurations are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 and Table A.3 add an analysis testing how determinant commutation affects runtime and memory feasibility as sequence size increases. Existing loss ablations, noise robustness tests, parameter sensitivity analyses, learning curves, and segmentation case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds with means and standard deviations for the principal experiments and noise tests, and three seeds for Figure 5. The added tables introduce no new repeated-run, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds substantial comparative results, including DINOv2-based TR2C accuracies of 98.6% on Weiz and 90.2% on Keck. Table A.3 adds timing and out-of-memory outcomes, including 28.0 versus 1039.3 ms/iteration with and without commutation at N = 1000. Tables 2–6 and matched appendix result tables retain their numerical entries; these additions are not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1's Appendix A Proposition 1 and its complete ridge-regression connection proof, Equations (15)–(27), are removed rather than relocated. v2 instead adds determinant-computation complexity reasoning in Appendix A.6 and corrects the loss definition in Equation (14). The removal materially changes the paper's formal theoretical support.

C1.justification: The central claims remain joint learning of temporally consistent UoS representations and affinity, first application of MCR2 to temporal-sequence clustering, and superior HMS performance across five datasets and different features. Consolidating the contribution bullets and explaining component roles in the conclusion do not change these claims' substantive scope.

C2.justification: The unchanged TAS results are reframed from 'Limitation and failure cases' into a comparison between HMS and TAS. v2 removes the assertion that fine-grained manipulative actions cannot be effectively captured by UoS, materially weakening the stated applicability boundary. It also interprets the new feature comparisons as showing that TR2C faithfully reflects DINOv2 > CLIP > HoG feature quality.

D1.justification: v2 adds a TR2C code-availability statement and link, a HoG feature-access link, ViT-L/14 model identifiers, and TAS-method tuning grids in Table A.7. Appendix A.6 also documents determinant computation. The earlier HMS and TAS hyperparameter tables are retained after renumbering; these disclosures do not establish changes to the original implementations.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning deep subspace clustering collapse, structured sparse subspace clustering, graph-convolution oversmoothing, DINOv2, and HVQ. Four rigid-motion references accompanying the former limitation discussion are removed. These changes extend contextual positioning while retaining the central relationship to MCR2 and HMS research.

P1.justification: v2 edits sentences and terminology throughout the main text, consolidates the contribution list, moves dataset descriptions from Section 4.1 to Appendix A.1, reorganizes the supplementary sections, and adds acknowledgments. The main narrative structure and much of the supplementary prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is revised, Figure 3 and Appendix Figure A.2 gain numerical bar annotations, and Figure 4 replaces separate EnSC/LSR axes with one ACC axis per panel. Tables 7, A.3, and A.7 are added, and existing displays are relocated or reformatted. The overall layout and most graphical content remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The loss-sign correction resolves an internal inconsistency, while Table 7 strengthens comparative evaluation and the new timing study, access information, and tuning grids improve empirical support and reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by removal of the auxiliary proof and the explicit fine-grained-action limitation; the retained TAS scores do not establish that this limitation was resolved. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
